2027-06-24.title: The Birth of John the Baptist · Thursday of the fifth week after Pentecost
readings: Pursue peace with everyone, and the holiness without which no one will see the Lord
“His name is John”: the birth of the forerunner
Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you, and imitate their faith
The faithful and wise servant whom the master finds at work
2027-06-24.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Fifth Sunday after Pentecost, in the Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu), which ends on 29 June. The Panchangam keeps today the Birth of John the Baptist (Yohannan Mamdana), with Hebrews 12:14–17 and Luke 1:57–66. It also keeps the memory of Cheppattu Philipose Ramban, with its own pair of readings (Hebrews 13:7–16; Matthew 24:45–51). A Ramban is a celibate monk-priest of the Syriac tradition; the Panchangam gives no further details of his life.
theo: The Church keeps the earthly birthday of very few saints. For most, she celebrates the day of their death, their birth into heaven. But she keeps the birth of Christ, the birth of his Mother, and the birth of John the Baptist, whom our tradition calls Yohannan Mamdana, John the Baptizer. St Augustine already remarked that the Church honours only two births with a solemn feast in his day, that of the Lord and that of John, because John's birth was itself part of the good news (Sermon 287, in substance). Before he was born, the angel told Zechariah: “even before his birth he will be filled with the Holy Spirit.” And when the Mother of God, carrying the Lord in her womb, came to greet Elizabeth, “the child leaped in her womb.” The forerunner was sanctified by the presence of Christ before he saw the light of day. The feast falls six months before Christmas, as Luke's Gospel suggests, and Augustine noticed that after John's birth the days of the northern year begin to shorten, while after Christ's birth they begin to lengthen: the creation itself seems to repeat John's words, “He must increase, but I must decrease” (John 3:30; Augustine, Sermons on the Nativity of John, in substance).

St Luke tells the birth simply: “Now the time came for Elizabeth to give birth, and she bore a son. Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown his great mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her.” An old couple who had waited all their lives now hold a child, and the whole village shares their joy. Then comes the naming. “On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they were going to name him Zechariah after his father.” In our own families it is the custom to name the first son after his grandfather, and everyone knows the quarrels that can follow when parents choose otherwise. Elizabeth breaks the custom: “No; he is to be called John.” The relatives object: “None of your relatives has this name.” They turn to Zechariah, who has been silent for nine months since he doubted the angel in the temple. “He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, ‘His name is John.’ And all of them were amazed.” The name was not the family's choice but God's, and it means that the Lord has shown favour. The moment Zechariah obeys, his silence ends: “Immediately his mouth was opened and his tongue freed, and he began to speak, praising God.” The tongue that was tied by doubt is loosened by obedience, and its first words are praise.

The neighbours were filled with awe, and the news ran through the hill country of Judea. “All who heard them pondered them and said, ‘What then will this child become?’ For, indeed, the hand of the Lord was with him.” That question is asked over every cradle and at every baptismal font. This month, as the schools of Kerala reopen in the rain and children set out with new books and new uniforms, parents ask it again: what will this child become? John became a prophet of the desert, whose food was locusts and wild honey, a man of prayer and fasting who prepared a people for the Lord. It is fitting that his feast falls within the Apostles' Fast, for he prepared the Apostles too: St John's Gospel tells us that Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was first a disciple of John, and that it was John who pointed him to Jesus with the words “Look, here is the Lamb of God!” (John 1:36). The greatest of the prophets was the one who sent his own disciples away from himself to Christ.

The Epistle of the feast gives the shape of such a life: “Pursue peace with everyone, and the holiness without which no one will see the Lord.” Holiness is not a decoration for a few; it is the road by which anyone at all comes to see God. The letter warns against “a root of bitterness” (Hebrews 12:15) that springs up and defiles many, and against becoming “like Esau, an immoral and godless person, who sold his birthright for a single meal.” John never sold his birthright. He would not claim to be the Messiah when the crowds wanted him to, and he would not keep silent before Herod when silence would have saved his life. The fast trains us in the same freedom of heart: to refuse the single meal, the comfort, the flattery, for which we might trade our place as children of God. Today the Panchangam also remembers Cheppattu Philipose Ramban, and gives for his memory the words, “Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.” We know little of him beyond his name and his title, but the Church asks us to remember those monks, priests and teachers who handed on the faith in our land, and to be, like them and like John, faithful servants whom the Master finds at work when he comes.
outline: Ask: what did my parents hope I would become, and what does God hope I will become?
Point 1 · A birth that is good news
Why the Church celebrates the birthday of John, the forerunner sanctified before birth.
God's name over the family's custom; Zechariah's obedience and his loosened tongue.
Point 3 · “What then will this child become?”
The prophet of the desert who prepared the Apostles and pointed them to the Lamb.
Point 4 · Holiness without which no one will see the Lord
Not selling our birthright for a single meal; the faithful leaders we remember.
“He must increase, but I must decrease.”
live: Bring one decision you are making this week, about study, work or family, before God in prayer, and be ready to write “His name is John” where he asks.
Pray Zechariah's canticle, Luke 1:68–79, each morning until the feast of Sts Peter and Paul.
Pull up a root of bitterness (Hebrews 12:15)
Make peace this week with one relative with whom you have quarrelled.
2027-06-24.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Lamb of God, your forerunner John leaped for joy in his mother's womb at the greeting of your holy Mother, and his birth filled his parents and neighbours with gladness. As you loosened the tongue of Zechariah when he obeyed your word, open our lips to praise you. Give us the holiness without which no one will see you, keep us from every root of bitterness, and let us never sell our birthright for a single meal. Bless the children of our families as they begin a new school year, and let your hand be with them as it was with John. Through the prayers of John the Baptist, and in memory of your servant Philipose Ramban and of all who spoke your word to us, make us faithful servants, ready for your coming. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: In many liturgies the Church repeats the words of John the Baptist as the Lamb of God is shown to us, and like John we point away from ourselves to the One who takes away the sin of the world and gives himself as our food.
conn: Isaiah 49:1 and Jeremiah 1:5 speak of prophets called and named before birth; Luke 1:15 and 1:41 show John filled with the Holy Spirit and leaping for joy in the womb at the greeting of the Mother of God.
Malachi 4:5 promises the prophet Elijah before the day of the Lord; Jesus says of John in Matthew 11:14, “he is Elijah who is to come.”
John 1:35–42: Andrew and another disciple of John follow Jesus, and Andrew brings his brother Simon; the Apostles' Fast keeps the memory of those whom John helped prepare.
fathers: John is the voice, Christ is the Word: the voice passes once it has carried the word, but the Word remains for ever; John was a voice for a time, Christ was the Word in the beginning (Sermon 293, in substance).

Zechariah's tongue was loosed when he wrote the name, because the voice of praise is given back to those who obey; the grace that the name John signifies opened his mouth (Homilies on the Gospels, on the Nativity of John, in substance).
magis: St John the Baptist is the Lord's immediate precursor or forerunner, sent to prepare his way; “prophet of the Most High”, he surpasses all the prophets, of whom he is the last, and he inaugurates the Gospel, already from his mother's womb welcoming the coming of Christ and rejoicing in being the friend of the bridegroom (in substance).

John was filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother's womb by Christ himself, whom the Virgin Mary had just conceived by the Holy Spirit; Mary's visitation to Elizabeth thus became a visit from God to his people (in substance).
All the faithful, of whatever rank or status, are called to the fullness of the Christian life and to the perfection of charity (in substance).

quick: Elizabeth gives birth to a son, and her neighbours and relatives rejoice at the mercy the Lord has shown her.
Against family custom the child is named John, as the angel had said; Zechariah writes “His name is John”, and his tongue is loosened to praise God.
The Epistle calls us to pursue peace and the holiness without which no one will see the Lord; the Panchangam also remembers Cheppattu Philipose Ramban.
2027-06-24.action: Pray the Benedictus, the canticle of Zechariah (Luke 1:68–79), slowly today.
2027-06-24.question: What does God want me to become, and am I letting him write my name?

family.explain: Zechariah and Elizabeth were old and had no children, and God gave them a baby. Everyone wanted to call him Zechariah, like his father. But God had already chosen his name: John, which means God is kind. Zechariah could not speak, so he wrote on a tablet: His name is John! At once he could speak again, and the first thing he did was to praise God. John grew up to be the one who showed people Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for all the children of our family and our parish as the new school year begins, that God's hand may be with them.
family.ask: Ask: “Why was your name chosen? Let us thank God for the name each of us received at Baptism.”

illus: In a family near Kottayam the first grandson was born, and the grandfather, a strong-willed man, announced at once that the boy would carry his name, as the custom was. The young parents had prayed through a difficult pregnancy and had promised to name the child after the saint whose intercession they had asked. For some days the house was tense. On the day of the baptism, the grandfather stood beside the font and heard the priest ask, What name do you give this child? The father answered with the saint's name. Afterwards, at lunch, the old man stood up, raised his glass of water, and said: I wanted the child to carry my name; but I have been thinking of Zechariah, who had to write a name he had not chosen. Let the boy carry the name God gave him, and let him carry my blessing too. The family says it was the best speech he ever made.

pm.open: Lord God, you gave John to Zechariah and Elizabeth as a sign of your great mercy. Open our lips to praise you, and let your hand be on us and on our children. Amen.
share: Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown his great mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her (Luke 1:58). When have I rejoiced with someone at the mercy God showed them?
He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, His name is John (Luke 1:63). Where is God asking me to obey him rather than custom or opinion?
What then will this child become? (Luke 1:66). What do I hope for the children I know, and do I pray for them?
pm.resp: Lord, let your hand be with us.
interc: For the Church, that like John the Baptist she may always point to Christ, the Lamb of God.
For children and young people beginning the new school year, that the hand of the Lord may be with them.
For couples waiting for a child, that they may know the mercy God showed to Zechariah and Elizabeth.
For the monks, priests and teachers who spoke the word of God to us, especially Cheppattu Philipose Ramban whose memory we keep, that the Lord may reward them.
For all who keep the Apostles' Fast, that they may pursue peace and holiness and never sell their birthright for a single meal.
pm.close: Lord God, you sent John the Baptist to prepare the way for your Son. Give your Church the joy of his birth, the courage of his witness and the humility of his heart, so that Christ may increase in us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: The Syriac word for the Baptizer, from the verb meaning to baptize. In the Syro-Malankara and other Syriac traditions John the Baptist is called Yohannan Mamdana, John the Baptizer.
kidsaint: When the baby was born, everyone wanted to call him Zechariah, like his father. His father could not speak, because he had doubted the angel's message. So he asked for a writing tablet and wrote in big letters: His name is John. At that very moment his mouth was opened, and he began to praise God! Lesson: when we obey God, even in small things, our hearts and our mouths are opened to praise him.

homily: Dear friends, today we celebrate a birthday. The Church keeps the birthday of very few saints, but she keeps the birth of John the Baptist, because his birth was part of the good news. Before he was born he was filled with the Holy Spirit, and when the Mother of God came to visit Elizabeth, the child leaped in her womb (Luke 1:41).

St Luke tells us that when Elizabeth bore a son, her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown his great mercy to her, and they rejoiced with her (Luke 1:58). Then they wanted to name the child after his father. But Elizabeth said: No; he is to be called John (Luke 1:60). And Zechariah, who had been silent for months, asked for a writing tablet and wrote, His name is John (Luke 1:63). At once his mouth was opened and he began to speak, praising God (Luke 1:64). Obedience opened his lips, and his first words were praise.

The people asked: What then will this child become? For, indeed, the hand of the Lord was with him (Luke 1:66). John became the voice in the desert, the man of fasting and prayer who prepared the way of the Lord and pointed his own disciples to Jesus. Some of the Apostles were first his disciples. In this Apostles' Fast we thank God for him.

The Epistle tells us how to follow him: Pursue peace with everyone, and the holiness without which no one will see the Lord (Hebrews 12:14). Do not be like Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal (Hebrews 12:16). Today we also remember Cheppattu Philipose Ramban and all who spoke the word of God to us. Let us imitate their faith, let us pray for our children, and let us say with John: He must increase, but I must decrease. Amen.
kids: Children, today is the birthday of John the Baptist! His parents were very old, and God gave them a baby as a surprise. Everyone wanted to call him by his father's name, but God had chosen the name John. His father wrote it on a little board: His name is John! When John grew up, he told everyone: Look, there is Jesus, the Lamb of God! You have just begun a new school year. Like John, you can help your friends to know Jesus, by being kind and by praying for them.

intro: On the Birth of John the Baptist (Yohannan Mamdana), within the Apostles' Fast, with the memory of Cheppattu Philipose Ramban: the forerunner sanctified before birth, the name given by God, the prophet who prepared the Apostles, and the holiness without which no one will see the Lord.

sub: God's name over the family's custom.
The name means that the Lord has shown favour.
q: The Lord called me before I was born, while I was in my mother's womb he named me.
Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you will name him John.
points.apply: Bring one plan of yours before God this week and ask him what name he wants to write on it.

sub: Nine months of silence after doubt.
The Benedictus, the morning song of the Church.
q: O Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare your praise.
Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he has looked favorably on his people and redeemed them.
points.apply: Pray the canticle of Zechariah each morning until the feast of the Apostles.

sub: The hand of the Lord was with him.
The prophet of the desert and the fast.
The friend of the bridegroom who sent his disciples to the Lamb.
q: Lo, I will send you the prophet Elijah before the great and terrible day of the Lord comes.
He must increase, but I must decrease.
points.apply: Pray by name this week for the children of your family as they begin the school year.

points.h: Holiness without which no one will see the Lord
sub: Esau's single meal and John's faithfulness.
Remembering those who spoke the word of God to us.
q: Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
points.apply: Make peace with one relative, and pray for the priests and teachers who handed on the faith to you.

concl: John's birth is good news: God is gracious, and the forerunner of the Lamb has come.
Like John, we are called to holiness, to praise, and to point away from ourselves to Christ.
2027-06-24.resolve: Let God name your life, open your lips in praise, and let Christ increase in you.
